proposal: 776BC Content & Copy Skill for Claude (776BC), 30 September 2026, v1.1
consent: I approve the 776BC Content & Copy Skill for Claude proposal dated 30 September 2026: up to 20 hours of implementation and a four-week controlled pilot for a fixed fee of A$5,000 ex GST, payable 50% on approval and commencement and 50% on release of the Skill to the controlled pilot.
scope: Up to 20 hours of Claude Skill implementation over two weeks, followed by a four-week controlled pilot
payment_milestones: 50% on approval and commencement; 50% on release of the Skill to the controlled pilot
approval_type: Approval of the proposal, including its stated scope, fixed fee and payment terms
proposal_text: 01 Purpose Following your review of 776BC’s approach to AI-supported copywriting, I recommend adapting the proposed Calliope pilot into a native Claude Skill. The objective is to give the 776BC team a simple, repeatable way to create and review selected content inside Claude while protecting the human authorship that underpins the authenticity of the brand. The Skill will review copy against the approved 776BC brand canon and produce website, print collateral and social copy. Campaigns, blogs and articles remain human-authored: the Skill may review them but not write them. Every output requires human approval before it is published. This approach removes the need for an external Telegram, Slack or Teams interface. The commercial investment remains unchanged. The effort previously allocated to channel integration will instead be directed towards brand-canon preparation, authorship controls, skill development, evaluation and team deployment. Recommended decision Approve the 20-hour Claude Skill implementation and controlled pilot. Engagement parameters PlatformClaudeNative Skill Build period2 weeks Controlled pilot4 weeks Effort20 hours Fixed feeA$5,000ex GST Revision note This proposal replaces the Calliope Telegram Pilot proposal dated 4 September 2026. 02 What the Skill does The team will use one capability within Claude: the 776BC Content & Copy Skill. It identifies the type of content being requested and applies the appropriate operating mode. Content typeReview permittedCreation permittedRewriting permitted Website copyYesYesYes Campaign copyYesNoNo Print collateralYesYesYes Social copyYesYesYes Blogs and articlesYesNoNo Copy review The Skill assesses submitted copy against the 776BC brand canon. It returns an overall assessment, brand-alignment scoring, strengths to preserve, issues ranked by importance and a recommendation on readiness for approval. It flags prohibited or off-brand language and unsupported claims. For campaigns, blogs and articles, Claude acts as a critic rather than a co-writer. It diagnoses and advises without returning publishable replacement copy. Approved copywriting For website, collateral and social content, the Skill creates and revises copy using the approved brand canon, relevant source material and the user’s brief. Generated drafts remain subject to human review and approval. Where a request is ambiguous, the Skill will seek clarification or default to the more conservative review-only mode. The Skill will not attempt to remove, alter or circumvent Claude’s content-marking mechanisms. 03 How it is delivered This is not simply the creation of a general prompt. The existing 776BC vault holds substantial brand intelligence that must be assessed, curated and translated into a focused Claude capability. Only the material required for the agreed use cases will be included. WorkstreamOutcomeHours Confirm the authorship policyA working session to confirm the five content classifications, the boundary between website and campaign copy, what Claude may do when reviewing human-authored work, approval responsibilities and the initial users.2 Prepare the approved brand knowledgeA controlled subset of the canon covering voice, style, vocabulary, prohibited terms, claims and channel behaviour, with conflicting or outdated instructions identified.4 Design and build the Claude SkillA Skill that classifies each request, applies the authorship rule, references the approved canon and explains when a request has been limited.6 Evaluation and refinementTesting of output quality and boundary behaviour, including ambiguous requests and attempts to override the authorship policy. Material issues are corrected before release.4 Deployment and handoverInstallation package, user guide and team handover. Sharing options depend on the 776BC Claude account structure; individual accounts may require separate installation by each user.2 Controlled pilot and final refinementFour weeks of use on real 776BC content tasks, followed by consolidated refinement from prioritised feedback.2 Total20 hours Delivery sequence Week 1 Policy and preparation Kick-off, authorship policy, brand material and an initial working version. Week 2 Build and release Skill development, evaluation, installation and team handover. Weeks 3 to 6 Controlled pilot Team pilot, feedback capture, final refinement and a pilot review with recommendation. The implementation will commence once the proposal is approved, the initial payment is received and the required Claude and source-material access is available. 04 What you receive One 776BC Content & Copy Skill for Claude, with review and copywriting modes Encoded human-authorship policy Curated 776BC brand reference set Copy-review and scoring framework Installation package and user guide Four-week controlled pilot Up to two hours of post-pilot refinement Recommended next steps following the pilot The pilot succeeds when The Skill correctly identifies the agreed content categories across the release test set Campaigns, blogs and articles remain in review-only mode Website, collateral and social requests produce usable first drafts Reviews identify brand-language violations and give clear, actionable guidance Nominated users can install and use the Skill reliably Human approval remains mandatory Claude Skills guide model behaviour rather than operating as a technically locked publishing system. Model outputs can vary between requests. Human approval therefore remains a mandatory part of the operating model. 05 Not included Telegram, Slack or Microsoft Teams integration Social-media scheduling, CMS integration or automated publishing Creation of campaign copy, blogs or articles Live access to the complete 776BC vault, or changes to Flowstate, Workbench or n8n Legal verification of marketing claims Claude subscription or account fees Ongoing content production, or support beyond the included pilot refinement Any additional integration, content category or workflow will be scoped separately before work begins. 06 Investment and terms Fixed project fee A$5,000 excluding GST The fee covers up to 20 hours of design, development, testing, deployment and included pilot refinement. Payment terms 50% on approval and commencement 50% on release of the Skill to the controlled pilot Additional work requires prior written approval Approved additional work is billed at A$250 per hour excluding GST This proposal is valid for 14 days. Intellectual property 776BC retains ownership of its existing brand material, source content and confidential business information. Following full payment, 776BC will receive an ongoing internal-use licence for the completed 776BC-specific Skill package, curated brand references and operating documentation. The Skill may not be resold, redistributed or provided to third parties as a standalone product without written agreement. OptiFlows retains ownership of its pre-existing and reusable methods, frameworks, evaluation approaches, underlying templates, implementation techniques and general know-how. Detailed implementation logic, working materials and proprietary evaluation methods are produced as part of the engagement and are not transferred through this proposal document.
